analysis.investment_thesis: NEPHROPLUS operates in an attractive chronic-disease niche with 27.5% revenue CAGR, but at a 3.1% earnings yield (EBIT ₹167 Cr / EV ₹5,392 Cr) it fails the Magic Formula's most basic valuation test. The business is improving but the market has already priced in years of future growth at a 74.7x P/E.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 27.5% (2021-2025) with operating income exploding from ₹37 Cr to ₹167 Cr — clear operating leverage kicking in
ROIC ~19-20% (EBIT ₹167 Cr / capital employed ~₹850 Cr) is approaching the Magic Formula's 20% threshold
Sticky recurring revenue model — dialysis is a non-discretionary, life-sustaining treatment with high patient retention
key_risks: Earnings Yield of only 3.1% — nearly 4x below the 12% Magic Formula hurdle; you are overpaying massively for growth
Capex-heavy expansion: ₹101 Cr capex vs ₹135 Cr OCF in 2025, FCF only just turned positive (₹35 Cr) after years of destruction
Fragile profitability history — net losses in 2022 (-₹21 Cr) and 2023 (-₹12 Cr); one operational setback could push it back to loss-making
red_flags: Earnings Yield 3.1% — well below Magic Formula's 6% minimum threshold
Net profit was negative as recently as FY2023; insufficient earnings history for reliable ROIC calculation
P/E of 74.7x for a business with ROCE of only 14.1% — growth is priced in but not yet structurally proven
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula on NEPHROPLUS: EBIT = ₹167 Cr (FY2025 operating income), Enterprise Value = Market Cap ₹5,260 Cr + Debt ₹258 Cr - Cash ₹126 Cr = ₹5,392 Cr. Earnings Yield = 3.1% — catastrophically below the 12% threshold I look for and even below the 6% "don't bother" cutoff. On the quality side, ROIC of ~19-20% (EBIT/Capital Employed) is approaching acceptable, but ROCE of 14.1% reported tells a more muted story once you account for all capital including lease liabilities typical in a clinic-chain model. One metric is borderline decent; the other is disqualifying.

The business narrative is genuinely interesting — dialysis is a chronic, recurring, non-discretionary service with 27.5% revenue growth and real operating leverage (operating income 4.5x in 4 years). But the market knows this and has priced it at 74.7x trailing earnings and 22.5x EV/EBITDA. For the Magic Formula to work, I need to buy good businesses at bargain prices — not pay a luxury price for a business that only recently emerged from losses. Free cash flow just turned positive at ₹35 Cr in FY2025 against a ₹5,260 Cr market cap (0.7% FCF yield). Pass.
